accepted.question_text: For a general isolated hypersurface singularity in C^n defined by the germ of a holomorphic function F, the Mather-Yau theorem says that the singularity is determined up to biholomorphism by n and the isomorphism class of the Tjurina algebra T_F = C[[z_1, ..., z_n]]/(F, F_{z_1}, ..., F_{z_n}). How can one explicitly reconstruct the singularity from this Tjurina algebra?

evidence.quote: In fact, for a general isolated hypersurface singularity in C^n defined by (the germ of) a holomorphic function F, the Mather-Yau theorem states that, remarkably, the singularity is determined, up to biholomorphism, by n and the isomorphism class of the Tjurina algebra T_F := C[[z1, . . . , zn]]/(F, Fz1, . . . , Fzn).
The proof of the Mather-Yau theorem is not constructive, and it is an important open problem-called the reconstruction problem-to understand explicitly how the singularity is
encoded in the corresponding Tjurina algebra.

accepted.question_text: Let X_n^d be the space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n with nonzero discriminant, and let Phi assign to each such form its associated form of degree n(d-2) on the dual space. For every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d, does there exist a rational GL_n-invariant function R on the space of degree n(d-2) associated forms, defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), such that R composed with Phi equals S?

evidence.quote: The principal object of our study is the morphism Φ : Xd_n → C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2), f 7→ f of affine algebraic varieties, where Xd_n is the variety of forms in C[z1, . . . , zn]d with nonzero discriminant.

Conjecture 1.1. For every regular GLn-invariant function S on Xd_n there exists a rational GLn-invariant function R on C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) defined at all points of the set Φ(Xd_n) ⊂ C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) such that R ◦ Φ = S.

accepted.question_text: For every n >= 2 and d >= 3, prove both of the following conditions used to establish Conjecture 1.1: first, the morphism P∇|P X_n^d from P X_n^d // SL_n to Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n is a closed immersion, meaning an isomorphism onto a closed subset; second, the morphism PΨ from Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n to P C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}^{ss} // SL_n is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset.

evidence.quote: Factorization (3.3) yields that in order to show that the map PΦ satisfies the condition stated in Claim 3.1, it suffices to prove the following: (C1) P∇|PXd_n is a closed immersion, i.e., an isomorphism onto a closed subset of Z^{d−1}_n // SLn; (C2) PΨ is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset of PC[e1, . . . , en]ss_{n(d−2)}// SLn.
Open Problem 3.2. Prove that conditions (C1) and (C2) are satisfied for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: Let P∇ be the morphism induced by sending a degree-d form f to the span of its first partial derivatives in the Grassmannian Gr(n, C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1}), and then passing to GIT quotients by SL_n. Is the image of P∇|P X_n^d normal for all n >= 2 and d >= 3?

evidence.quote: The gradient morphism ∇ introduced in (2.19) indices the morphism Wd_n → Gr(n, C[z1, . . . , zn]d−1), f 7→ hfz1, . . . , fzni, where h · i denotes linear span. This morphism descends to an SLn-equivariant morphism P∇: PWd_n → Gr(n, C[z1, . . . , zn]d−1).
Open Problem 3.4. Show that the image of P∇|PXd_n is normal for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: For n >= 2 and d >= 3, can one find a homogeneous SL_n-invariant on C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} whose nonvanishing locus contains, as a closed subset, the set U_n^{n(d-2)} of degree n(d-2) forms F such that F^perp intersected with C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1} is n-dimensional and has a basis with nonvanishing resultant?

evidence.quote: Let U^{n(d−2)}_n ⊂ C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) be the locus of forms F such that the subspace F⊥ ∩ C[z1, . . . , zn]d−1 is n-dimensional and has a basis with nonvanishing resultant.

Open Problem 3.10. Show that for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 3 one can find a homogeneous SLn-invariant on the space C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2) such that U^{n(d−2)}_n is a closed subset of the complement to its zero locus.

accepted.question_text: Let Phi be the associated-form map from nondegenerate homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n to homogeneous degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space. Repeated application of this construction gives iterates such as Phi^2 when defined as rational maps between the corresponding spaces of forms. Is Phi^k a well-defined rational map for every positive integer k?

evidence.quote: The principal object of our study is the morphism Φ : Xd_n → C[e1, . . . , en]n(d−2), f 7→ f of affine algebraic varieties, where Xd_n is the variety of forms in C[z1, . . . , zn]d with nonzero discriminant.

The existence of such a form also insures that one can consider the iteration Φ2, viewed as a rational map from C[z1, . . . , zn]d to C[z1, . . . , zn]n(n(d−2)−2). This observation leads to the following natural question: Open Problem 3.16. Is the iteration Φk a well-defined rational map for all k ∈ N?

accepted.question_text: For the associated-form morphism Phi, define p to be the smallest positive integer such that Delta^p Phi extends from the nondegenerate locus X_n^d to a morphism on the entire affine space of degree-d forms. Compute this integer p.

evidence.quote: Let p := max{pi1,...,in : i1 + · · · + in = n(d − 2)}. Then the product ∆pΦ is the morphism ∆pΦ: Xd_n → C[z∗_1, . . . , z∗_n]n(d−2), f 7→ ∆(f)^pΦ(f), which extends to a morphism from C[z1, . . . , zn]d to C[z∗_1, . . . , z∗_n]n(d−2).
Open Problem 5.1. Compute the integer p.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist any pair (n, d) for which the minimal exponent p needed to extend Delta^p Phi to all degree-d forms is strictly greater than 1?

evidence.quote: Observe that for n = 2, 3 upper bound (5.2) yields p = 1. However, (5.2) is not sharp in general.
Open Problem 5.5. Is there an example with p > 1?
